task.name: Invocation ledger recording configured, resolved, and billed model identity with usage
task.story_text:
## Why

An invocation currently collapses several distinct facts into one. The model a run was configured
to use, the concrete version that configuration resolved to at invocation time, and the models
actually billed within that invocation are three different things, and a single invocation can
have a different answer for each — a strong-tier configuration can resolve to one concrete version
and bill a smaller component model alongside it.

Recording one identity per invocation forces a choice among the three and discards the rest. The
adaptive router then attributes outcome and cost evidence to whichever one survived, which is
neither the thing the operator selected nor the complete set of things that were paid for.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every agent invocation records the configured identity, the resolved primary identity, and each
  billed component identity as separate values rather than one collapsed value.
- Each invocation records role, complexity, reasoning effort, usage counts by class, and observed
  cost, and states whether that cost was reported by the provider or estimated.
- Indexed model identity is populated from these records, so a consumer reading the index sees the
  same identity the record carries.
- A consumer can attribute cost and outcome to the configured identity and to the resolved
  identity independently, and can tell when the two differ.
- Records written before this ledger remain readable, and a consumer can tell a record that
  carries the full set from one that does not.

## Example

A single dev invocation configured as a strong-tier alias currently reduces to one ambiguous
identity, discarding the rest:

```
configured        opus                          (what the operator selected)
resolved primary  claude-opus-5                 (what the alias became at invocation time)
billed components claude-opus-5      $10.892
                  claude-haiku-4-5   $0.010     (billed, never configured, absent from the catalog)
```

Today the last group is the only place any of this survives, the first two are not recorded
together anywhere, and the indexed identity is empty.

handoff.summary: Added a first-class per-invocation identity ledger. AgentResult/ModelUsage gained configured_model, configured_transport, reasoning_effort, and cost_provenance; runners stamp provenance at their cost sites (Claude CLI result event = provider_reported, kill-path reconstruction / Codex / gh-aw / all API adapters = estimated, unmeasured = unknown) and cli.run_agent stamps the configured half at the single dispatch seam. audit_render.build_invocation_ledger renders a versioned block with configured_identity, resolved_primary_identity, billed_components[], role/complexity/reasoning_effort, usage counts by class, and cost provenance; build_agent_entries now covers preflight, plan, plan_review, dev, review and synthesis, and preflight_flow attaches a ledger to each individual preflight attempt so superseded parse-retries and fallbacks carry the same shape. agent_identity gained entry_identity_ledger/dev_identity_ledger with a full_ledger marker, and the existing single-identity projections now read resolved_primary_identity from the ledger while keeping their legacy reconstruction path byte-for-byte. Substrate schema 6->7 adds dev_configured_model(_resolution), dev_resolved_model(_resolution), dev_identity_ledger_version and dev_identity_ledger_full, re-derived for already-indexed history; escalation and assignment-history projections carry both identities plus the divergence and full-ledger markers. Record schema 20->21 with _migrate_v20_to_v21 that deliberately fabricates no ledger.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every agent invocation records the configured identity, the resolved primary identity, and each billed component identity as separate values rather than one collapsed value.
acceptance_criteria.notes: ledger.configured_identity / resolved_primary_identity / billed_components[] are three separate values, each with raw spelling plus canonical projection and resolution status. Coverage extends to every agent-invoking phase (preflight, plan, plan_review, dev, review, synthesis) and to each individual preflight attempt, not just the final one.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Each invocation records role, complexity, reasoning effort, usage counts by class, and observed cost, and states whether that cost was reported by the provider or estimated.
acceptance_criteria.notes: ledger carries role, complexity, complexity_score, reasoning_effort, usage {input,output,cache_read,cache_creation,thinking}, cost_usd and cost_provenance (provider_reported|estimated|unknown), with per-component provenance on each billed_component. Complexity is stamped from the run's preflight classification rather than from AgentResult, since the runner cannot know it; it is null on preflight attempts because that is what preflight is running to determine.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Indexed model identity is populated from these records, so a consumer reading the index sees the same identity the record carries.
acceptance_criteria.notes: _dev_identity_columns is the single projection used by both the write path (_flat_fields) and the repair path (_reindex_dev_model_identity), so the two cannot diverge. A seam test asserts the indexed dev_resolved_model equals the record's ledger.resolved_primary_identity.identity through a real run_task.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A consumer can attribute cost and outcome to the configured identity and to the resolved identity independently, and can tell when the two differ.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Separate index columns plus dev_configured_model/dev_resolved_model/dev_configured_differs_from_resolved on the escalation and assignment-history projections. Divergence is computed on the canonical projection when both sides canonicalize (so an alias is not reported as different from the version it names) and on raw spellings otherwise, and is null rather than false when either side is absent.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Records written before this ledger remain readable, and a consumer can tell a record that carries the full set from one that does not.
acceptance_criteria.notes: _migrate_v20_to_v21 fabricates nothing; entry_identity_ledger reports full_ledger:false for pre-ledger entries and the legacy single-identity read is asserted unchanged. The marker is indexed as dev_identity_ledger_full so the question is answerable by query.

story_deviations: Did not add a separate resolved_model field to AgentResult as Step 1 specified. model_used + transport_used already IS the resolved primary identity; a duplicate field would be a divergence risk with no new information. Only the configured half got new fields.

API-transport cost provenance is stamped at one seam (api._stamp_api_cost_provenance) instead of at each adapter's _estimate_cost call. No API adapter forge speaks returns a price, so the statement is a property of the transport rather than of any one provider — this also covers runner_gemini, which the plan reviewer flagged as omitted from Step 2's enumeration.

Dropped src/theforge/model_profiles.py from Step 6's file list, as the plan reviewer suggested. Adaptive routing still keys off the resolved identity; configured identity is carried alongside in the projections without changing any grouping today.
Complexity/complexity_score are stamped in the renderer from state.preflight_* rather than added to AgentResult, since runners have no access to the run's classification.
deferred_items: Gate not run (coordinator-owned). 22 test failures remain in six families — cut_rc_isolation, sprint_lock, run_setup, sprint_parallel, sprint_reexec_collision, sprint_run_id_rollover — all failing with PermissionError: Operation not permitted from multiprocessing/tempfile under the dev sandbox, plus run_setup's forge.yaml-sync assertions picking up this worktree's sprint-pinned snapshot. None touch the modules changed here; the coordinator's out-of-sandbox gate should confirm.

That file was restored to HEAD and the foreign stash remains intact at stash@{0} — worth an operator glance if that stash was expected to stay pending.

handoff.summary: Fixed the five gate failures, all caused by my own change. Rendering preflight into cost.agents routed state.preflight_result through _agent_entry's `assert isinstance(r, AgentResult)`. That field, unlike the phase-appended dev/review result lists, is a single reassigned field the rest of the writer already reads duck-typed (audit.py takes .cost_usd off it untyped), so a non-AgentResult value raised out of generate_audit_log and the run lost its entire audit record — which is why four test_sprint_parallel cases failed with a missing audit.yaml rather than a ledger assertion. build_agent_entries now gates the preflight entry on isinstance so an unreadable result costs one entry instead of the whole record and no entry is fabricated from an unknown object's attributes; preflight_flow._record_attempt got the symmetric guard recording an explicit null ledger. I fixed this in production code rather than rewriting the five sprint fixtures, because those fixtures are unrelated tests that use a MagicMock purely as a cost carrier, and editing them would have left the crash-site in place. Added a regression test pinning that a run with an unreadable preflight result still produces a complete audit record. I drafted and then deleted a test for the preflight_flow guard after verifying that branch is unreachable through the phase's own paths — it only re-asserted its own inlined copy of the guard, so the unreachability is recorded in a comment instead.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 adds fields inside audit list entries (agents[].ledger, billed_components[]). tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py pins element shapes for lists it considers stable (the #1997 rule), so the fixture must capture nested list element fields, not just top-level keys.
  Suggestion: When generating tests/fixtures/audit_record_schema_v21.json, regenerate it via the guard's own snapshot path rather than hand-authoring, and confirm agents[].ledger.billed_components[] element fields are recorded.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 enumerates runner_claude/codex/ghaw and the four adapters but omits src/theforge/runners/runner_gemini.py, which also produces AgentResult cost values.
  Suggestion: Include runner_gemini.py in the provenance-stamping sweep, or confirm its results flow through cli.py's central annotation so provenance is not left unknown for Gemini invocations.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 6 mentions src/theforge/model_profiles.py but the details only describe substrate/bridge projection changes; the concrete change to model_profiles.py is unspecified.
  Suggestion: Either state the specific configured-vs-resolved grouping change needed in model_profiles.py or drop it from the file list to keep the blast radius honest.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.4-cli] Step 3 assumes preflight can be handled like the other AgentResult lists, but in the real code the authoritative per-invocation preflight data lives in src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_flow.py:331-388 as attempts dicts embedded into state.preflight_result.raw['attempts'], while state.preflight_result itself keeps only the final attempt. Those dicts currently contain only profile_name/model/provider/cli/cost_usd/duration_s/success/exit_code/completed, and audit writing in src/theforge/coordinator/audit.py:794-834 just serializes them as-is. Without adding that capture site to the plan, earlier preflight parse-retries/fallbacks cannot record configured vs resolved identity, billed components, usage-class counts, reasoning effort, or cost provenance, so the 'every agent invocation' contract would still fail.
  Suggestion: Add an explicit step covering src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_flow.py (or a shared invocation-capture helper it uses) so each preflight attempt preserves the full ledger payload, then have audit.py/audit_render.py emit those per-attempt records instead of relying only on the rolled-up final state.preflight_result.
